title: Fast Bit-Sliced VLSI Architectures on FPGA for Montgomery Domain Modular Inversion
problem: Modular inversion computation forms a crucial component in Elliptic Curve Cryptosystems
motivation: Modular inversion computation forms a crucial component in Elliptic Curve Cryptosystems. In this paper, we have proposed a fast VLSI archi
method: The approach uses a hardware circuit design (VLSI) implemented on an FPGA—a reconfigurable chip—to speed up Kaliski's Montgomery domain modular inversion algorithm. Bit-slicing is the key technique: each bit of the data is processed through parallel hardware paths, allowing many computations to run simultaneously. Montgomery domain is a number representation that trades one-time conversion work for much faster repeated multiplications during the algorithm's execution. This hardware-software combination significantly accelerates modular inversion, a crucial operation in elliptic curve cryptography.
key_novelty: The core contribution is using bit-sliced parallel hardware design on FPGAs to accelerate Kaliski's Montgomery domain modular inversion.
